I found and fixed 12 rules out of 150 whose behaviour didn't match their docstrings. After the fixes, all 150 rules match the docstrings on every input I tested.

**How I checked:** I wrote a separate script that reads each rule's docstring (type, percentage, threshold, cap) and builds the correct result from it, following the shared rules in the module docstring. It then compared that against the real function for each rule. The inputs were quantities 0–159 plus larger values up to 5000, unit prices from 0 to 1,000,000, and negative inputs, which should raise an error. I also went through the file for any lines that don't follow the usual rule pattern. The other odd-looking lines, such as `if 10 <= qty` and `if disc > 100000: disc = 100000`, behave the same as the standard form, so I left them alone.

**What I fixed:**

| Rule | Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 21 | Cap applied only when the discount was over 60,000 | Always cap at 30,000 |
| 49 | Cap applied only when the discount was over 100,000 | Always cap at 50,000 |
| 27 | `qty > 30`, so 30 units got no discount | `qty >= 30` |
| 64 | `qty > 50` | `qty >= 50` |
| 65 | `qty >= 101` | `qty >= 100` |
| 77 | `qty >= 11` | `qty >= 10` |
| 94 | `qty >= 13` | `qty >= 12` |
| 76 | A "whole" rule using the "marginal" formula `(qty-100)*unit` | `base * 10 // 100` |
| 119 | A "whole" rule using the "marginal" formula `(qty-20)*unit` | `base * 5 // 100` |
| 115 | A "marginal" rule using the "whole" formula `base` | `(qty - 5) * unit * 15 // 100` |
| 104 | Capped the amount the percentage was applied to (at 50,000), not the discount | Work out the discount first, then cap it at 50,000 |
| 144 | Used `round()`, which rounds to nearest instead of flooring | `base * 3 // 100` |

I only changed calculation lines in `pricebook.py`; docstrings and other code are untouched. A copy of the original file is at `/tmp/chk/pricebook.orig.py`.

STATUS: DONE
